workload.execution: sdk::Node with caller-owned host/core runtimes, listeners, authenticated peer clients and object-store clients
workload.operation: transaction: increment persistent counter and overwrite JSON value with changing seeded random ASCII payload (64-symbol alphabet)
workload.load_model: closed loop; one in-flight request per worker; disjoint cell partitions; rotating ingress; no write retries
workload.latency: request start through complete HTTP response JSON; warmup excluded; percentile ranges across repetitions, not pooled percentiles
workload.build: Linux ARM64; Rust 1.98.1; repository release profile (opt-level=s, fat LTO)

limitations: All containers share one Apple M2 Max / Colima VM and backing disk; CPU affinity and quotas do not isolate disk or VM overhead.
RustFS is a local single-node S3-compatible store, not production S3 latency or durability.
The 5 GiB loop image has approximately 4.84 GiB usable ext4 capacity; it bounds node data, not the read-only container image.
Repeated overwrite workload with 10000 total cells; no growing dataset, hot-cell skew or long soak.
Each scenario uses a fresh bucket on a RustFS instance shared by the scenarios in that run.
Failures and rolling restarts occur between write phases; concurrent ambiguous write acknowledgements are not exercised.
Closed-loop measurements characterize saturation and do not correct coordinated omission for an independently arriving workload.
Fleet durability can fall back to bucket proof; peerlog files demonstrate replication, but acknowledgement source is not separately instrumented.
Raw verification 'nodes' records configured scenario width (3), not live process count; survivor and preserving-reload topology is established by selected endpoints and observed owners.
